title: Alberta Invites 425 Workers in Five Provincial Immigration Draws
excerpt: The Alberta Advantage Immigration Program issued 425 invitations across five draws between October 23 and November 2, led by the Rural Renewal Stream — but only 495 of the province's 6,603 nomination spaces for 2026 remain.
body:
• Alberta issued 425 invitations to apply for provincial nomination across five AAIP draws held between October 23 and November 2, 2026, with minimum scores between 50 and 60.
  • The Rural Renewal Stream accounted for 210 of the invitations; the Alberta Opportunity Stream issued 132 and the two Dedicated Health Care Pathway draws issued 83 combined.
  • An invitation is not a nomination: invitees must apply to AAIP, be approved, and then apply to the federal government for permanent residence — Express Entry nominees get 600 extra CRS points.
  • Time matters: Alberta had issued 6,108 of its 6,603 nominations for 2026 as of November 4, leaving 495 spaces, with 32,211 candidates still active in the expression-of-interest pool.

Alberta has invited 425 workers to apply for a provincial nomination in its latest round of draws, the Alberta Advantage Immigration Program (AAIP) confirmed in processing data updated on November 4. The five selection rounds, held between October 23 and November 2, targeted exactly the workers the province says it needs most: health-care staff, employees already working in Alberta, and newcomers willing to settle in designated rural communities.

Who was invited

The largest draw went to the Rural Renewal Stream, which invited 173 candidates on November 2 at a minimum score of 51 — the stream's biggest round since March 13, when 349 were invited. A smaller Rural Renewal draw on October 23 invited 37 candidates, also at 51; that was the stream's lowest invitation count of 2026. Rural Renewal candidates need a job offer from an employer in a designated Alberta community and an endorsement from that community.

The Alberta Opportunity Stream — for temporary foreign workers already employed full-time in Alberta — invited 132 candidates on October 30 at a minimum score of 59, five points higher than its previous draw on October 2. The Dedicated Health Care Pathway held two draws: 64 invitations through the non-Express Entry route on October 29 at a score of 50, the pathway's first such draw since August 19, and 19 through Express Entry on October 27 at 60, its smallest round of the year. The full draw table is published on the AAIP processing information page.

What an invitation does — and does not — do

An AAIP invitation is the start of the process, not the outcome. Invited candidates submit a full application to the province; only if AAIP approves it do they receive a nomination certificate, and nomination is what allows them to apply to the federal government for permanent residence. Candidates nominated through an Express Entry-linked pathway receive 600 additional Comprehensive Ranking System points, which in practice guarantees a federal invitation to apply. The province notes on its official processing page that draws are held as needed rather than on a fixed schedule, and that an expression-of-interest score is not the only factor in selection. CIC News' draw report puts the five rounds in the context of 95 AAIP selection rounds so far in 2026, with at least 14,584 candidates invited this year.

The narrowing window

The constraint for anyone still waiting in the pool is arithmetic. Alberta's 2026 nomination allocation is 6,603 — raised by 200 in August — and 6,108 nominations had been issued by November 4, leaving 495. Another 756 applications were in the queue to be processed. Against that, the worker expression-of-interest pool held 32,211 active profiles on November 4, including 20,603 in the Alberta Opportunity Stream alone, 1,283 in Rural Renewal and 976 in Health Care. Health care and Rural Renewal communities are two of Alberta's stated 2026 priorities, alongside technology, construction, manufacturing, aviation and agriculture — which is why four of these five draws landed in those two areas.

Separately from the 6,603 allocation, Alberta has also nominated 50 practice-ready physicians and 12 Francophone candidates under a federal initiative that does not count against the provincial cap. For Indian professionals already working in Alberta — a large share of the Opportunity Stream pool — the message of this round is that invitations are still flowing late in the year, but the remaining nomination spaces for 2026 are nearly gone.

steps.detail: An invitation is not a nomination. Invited candidates apply to the Alberta Advantage Immigration Program for a provincial nomination.
If AAIP approves the application, it issues a nomination. The process can take several months, and Alberta had 495 of its 6,603 nomination spaces for 2026 still remaining as of November 4.

steps.step: Apply to the federal government for permanent residence
steps.detail: Nominees apply to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada for PR. Express Entry nominees receive 600 additional CRS points, which in practice guarantees a federal invitation.
Nominees already in Canada who have submitted a PR application may qualify for a Bridging Open Work Permit while they wait.
